data.name: Gazzel Quest, The Five Magic Stones
data.detailed_description:
Gazzel is the bravest warrior of the armies of Pharaoh.
So tired of war, he decides to finish a life full of struggle and death.
But Pharaoh, furious with the decision of leaving by his best warrior, kidnaps his beloved Salama and orders to be imprisoned behind the Asorom door.
Asorom's door is sealed with the five sacred locks.
To open it, Gazzel must gather the five magical jewels.
Once all the jewels were placed in the five locks, the door will open and Samala will be free.
Every stone is kept by an underworld demon.
Our brave hero begins a dangerous journey through the five worlds with the only goal of bringing the five jewels together and open the evil door that retains his love.

The adventure is about to begin.

FEATURES

5 Amazing Stages
5 Gorgeous Bosses
More than 30 kinds of enemies
Awesome Music Themes
4 Different Weapons with 3 Levels of Power
Armours and Power ups
Pure OLD-SCHOOL GamePlay

reviews.review:
Gazzel Quest, The Five Magic Stones is a retro-styled action platformer developed and published by DemonVideogames. Built around the spirit of classic side-scrolling adventures, the game delivers a straightforward fantasy quest that prioritizes challenging gameplay and arcade-inspired action over cinematic storytelling. Its premise centers on Gazzel, a warrior who abandons a life of constant warfare in search of peace. His decision angers Pharaoh, who retaliates by kidnapping Gazzel’s beloved Salama and sealing her away behind the mysterious Asorom Door. To save her, Gazzel must embark on a dangerous journey to recover five magical stones guarded by powerful demonic forces.

The story itself is intentionally simple, serving mainly as motivation for the adventure ahead. Rather than overwhelming players with lengthy conversations or complex lore, the game quickly establishes its objective and throws them into a series of dangerous levels filled with enemies and hazards. This old-fashioned approach suits the title well, recalling an era when action games relied on gameplay and imagination more than narrative depth. While the plot is unlikely to leave a lasting emotional impact, it provides enough context to make the quest feel purposeful and engaging.

Gameplay is the core attraction. Players travel through five distinct stages, each featuring unique environments, enemy encounters, and a climactic boss battle. The adventure includes more than thirty enemy types, helping maintain variety throughout the campaign. Enemies possess different attack patterns and behaviors, encouraging players to learn their weaknesses and adapt accordingly. The challenge level remains consistent with classic platformers, rewarding patience, timing, and skillful movement rather than relying on modern conveniences.

Combat is enhanced by a selection of four weapons, each of which can be upgraded through multiple power levels. This system adds a welcome layer of progression, giving players a sense of growth as they advance through the game. Additional armor upgrades and power-ups further strengthen the character while providing incentives to explore levels thoroughly. These mechanics may be relatively simple by modern standards, but they fit the game’s retro identity and contribute to a satisfying gameplay loop.

Visually, Gazzel Quest embraces a colorful fantasy presentation. The environments are vibrant and varied enough to distinguish the five worlds from one another, while enemy and boss designs contribute to the game's adventurous atmosphere. The graphics are not particularly advanced, even by indie standards, but they effectively capture the charm of classic action titles. Players seeking cutting-edge visuals may find the presentation modest, yet those who appreciate nostalgic aesthetics will likely enjoy the game's visual style.

The soundtrack complements the experience with energetic themes that support exploration and combat. The music successfully reinforces the game's old-school character and helps maintain momentum throughout the adventure. Combined with the arcade-like gameplay, the audio design creates an experience that feels faithful to the genre inspirations that shaped the project.

One area where the game shows its limitations is originality. Many of its ideas draw heavily from classic platformers, and veterans of the genre may recognize familiar mechanics and design choices throughout the campaign. The relatively short length also means that the experience can be completed without a major time investment. However, the focused scope prevents the game from overstaying its welcome and allows it to remain consistently entertaining from start to finish.

Overall, Gazzel Quest, The Five Magic Stones is a charming retro action game that understands exactly what it wants to be. It offers a simple but enjoyable fantasy adventure filled with challenging platforming, varied enemies, weapon upgrades, and memorable boss encounters. While it lacks the innovation and production values of larger modern releases, it succeeds as a nostalgic tribute to classic action-platform games. Players who enjoy old-school gameplay, straightforward progression, and a healthy dose of retro challenge will likely find plenty to appreciate in Gazzel’s quest to rescue Salama and recover the legendary stones.

Rating: 6/10
